prompt: A team has a folder of polished components with colours written inside each one. What do they have?

choices.why: Right: the visible end, without the tokens or the rules.
Without tokens, a dark theme means editing every component.

choices.text: A token file in another format
choices.why: The colours are inside the components, not named once.

choices.text: A style guide for the brand
choices.why: A style guide is a document; this is code without shared decisions.

prompt: Why does this course treat a design system as a delivery problem?

choices.text: Because components are shipped as images
choices.why: They are shipped as code and tokens.
They do not; the pipeline does.
Right: a change made once reaches every screen that uses it, through a version and a build, with no screen edited by hand.

choices.text: Because it replaces the need for CI
choices.why: It adds checks to CI; it replaces nothing.

prompt: Match each token to its layer.
Which should a stylesheet refer to?

choices.why: That ties a meaning to one paint; a dark theme or a rebrand breaks it.
Right: the semantic token.
A literal is the thing tokens exist to remove.
A named colour is still a paint, not a meaning.

prompt: A developer needs a colour the semantic layer does not have. What should happen?

choices.why: That bypasses the layer that makes themes work.

choices.text: Write the hex in the stylesheet
choices.why: That is the drift a design system exists to stop.

choices.text: Add a component token for it
choices.why: A component token still needs a meaning above it.

choices.text: Ask for a semantic token to be added
choices.why: Right: it is a conversation about the system.

prompt: In `tokens.json`, what does `{color.grey-0}` mean?

choices.text: A colour named after a CSS keyword
choices.why: It is a reference, not a keyword.
Right: the primitive `grey-0` in the `color` group.

choices.text: A placeholder filled in by the browser
choices.why: The script resolves it before the browser sees anything.
JSON has no comments.

prompt: Why is `src/tokens.css` committed even though a script writes it?

choices.why: It can ignore anything.
It only reads it.

choices.text: Clones must build as they come
choices.why: Right: a fresh clone must build without running anything first, and a check that `npm run tokens` changes nothing keeps it honest.
They read the CSS the build produces.

prompt: In the Design Tokens Community Group format, a token's value is held under the key `___`.
With a base of 1rem and a ratio of 1.25, what is the third size, step 2, in rem? Answer with three decimals.
A marketing page wants headlines that dominate. Which ratio fits it best?

choices.why: That suits dense interfaces.
That is the planner's, for an app.
That suits articles and documentation.
Right: a perfect fifth.

prompt: Why are the sizes in `rem` rather than `px`?

choices.text: They follow the reader's own text setting
choices.why: Right: a larger default text scales the whole scale with it.

choices.text: `px` is not allowed in custom properties
choices.why: Any length is allowed.
Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: `rem` is the unit the ratio is written in
choices.why: The ratio has no unit.

prompt: The spacing unit is `0.25rem`. What is `--space-6`?

choices.why: The unit is a quarter rem, not a pixel.
Multiply, do not append.
That is `--space-8`.

prompt: Why does the planner keep `max-width: 40rem` as a plain value instead of a spacing token?

choices.text: Custom properties cannot be used in `max-width`
choices.why: They can be used in any property.
The lesson says why it stays.

choices.text: It is a column width, not space between things
choices.why: Right; forcing it onto the scale makes a token nobody can explain.
The number of steps is not the reason.

prompt: What contrast ratio does WCAG level AA ask for ordinary text?
`grey-400` passes on the dark page and fails on the dark raised panel. What does that show?

choices.text: The script measures the wrong thing
choices.why: It measured what the page draws.

choices.text: Check every surface it lands on
choices.why: Right, in every theme.
Every other dark pair passed.

choices.text: Raised panels should not have text
choices.why: The form sits on one.

prompt: What does the contrast script not check? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Colour used as the only signal
choices.why: Right: that needs a person.
Right: there is no single background.

choices.text: Muted text on the raised panel
choices.why: It checks that pair.
It checks every theme in the file.

prompt: A token change drops one pair to 4.27 and nobody notices in review. Which step would have stopped the merge?

choices.why: That writes the CSS; it measures nothing.
Types know nothing about colour.
A person looking at it is how it was missed.

choices.text: A required contrast step in CI
choices.why: Right: `npm run contrast` exits with an error, and the pipeline stops.

prompt: How does the planner's dark theme differ from its light theme in `style.css`?

choices.text: It does not: only the token values differ
choices.why: Right: same names, other values.

choices.text: A second block of rules for dark
choices.why: There is no such block in the stylesheet.
A filter would wreck the contrast the script measured.
One stylesheet serves both.

prompt: The system is dark, but the page sets `data-theme="light"` on the root. Which values apply?

choices.text: Dark, because the system preference wins
choices.why: The `:not([data-theme="light"])` exists to let the page override it.
Right: an explicit choice beats the system.

choices.text: Neither: the two conflict and nothing applies
choices.why: The selectors are written so they never conflict.

choices.text: Whichever block comes last in the file
choices.why: The dark block's selector excludes this element.

prompt: On a dark page, the date field stays white. What is missing?

choices.why: The browser draws the field; it ignores your tokens until told the page supports dark.
Right.
That changes custom properties, not the browser's own drawing.
Contrast is not why it is white.

prompt: What did `grep -nE '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,6}|[0-9]px' src/style.css; echo $?` print, and what does it mean?

choices.why: 0 would mean a match was found.
The file exists.

choices.text: `1`: no colour or pixel value is left
choices.why: Right: grep found nothing.
It searches for literals, not for tokens.

prompt: `style.css` starts with `@import "./tokens.css";`. How many stylesheet requests does the built page make?

choices.why: Right: Vite inlines the import into the one stylesheet it writes.
That is what a browser would do with an `@import` left in place.

choices.text: Two, plus one for each theme
choices.why: The themes are blocks inside the same file.

choices.text: None; the CSS is inside the script
choices.why: Vite writes it as a separate `.css` file.

choices.why: That throws away the layer that makes this a one-line change.
Two stylesheets drift apart.
